policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 6 May close (1x4 3.86, 3x6 3.99, 6x9 4.22, 9x12 4.40 vs WIBOR 3M 3.84) price roughly 55bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC held at 3.75% on 6 May (core probably rose in April; wait-and-see). Dąbrowski (30 Apr): the chance of cuts fell sharply after the April CPI. April flash CPI 3.2% (30 Apr; 3.0% expected); core 2.7% in March. The fuel VAT and excise cuts run to 15 May.
policy.risk_text: The hold anchors the front end at WIBOR while FRAs swing with Iran headlines (75bp priced within 10 months before the decision); long end: heavy May supply and a 6.5-6.8% deficit; a deal would unwind hike pricing.

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026; IMF (14 Apr): 2026 CPI 3.3%. The July projection is the next marker.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit 7.3% of GDP (GUS EDP, 22 Apr), debt 59.7%; 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; budget deficit after March PLN 69.6bn (25.6% of the limit); the fiscal notification and the government's assumptions put the 2026 deficit at ~6.8% of GDP; fuel package (VAT 8%, minimum excise, price caps) to 15 May.
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~49% (after 28 Apr, MoF) financed; budget accounts ~PLN 184bn at end-April (MoF estimate). S&P reviews Poland on 8 May (A-, stable; Erste sees a sizeable risk of a negative outlook); Fitch A- and Moody's A2 have negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP held at 3.75% on 6 May; April CPI 3.2% y/y; 2025 GDP 3.6%, Q4 4.1%. Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 6 May: the MPC held at 3.75% as expected; the statement says core probably rose in April and keeps wait-and-see; the June meeting moves to 1-2 June; PAP survey: a hold through 2026; the 10Y POLGB fell ~20bp on US-Iran deal hopes as the market pared hike bets after pricing 75bp within 10 months (ING). Abroad: the US paused the escorts and sent Iran a one-page memorandum to end the war: Brent -7.6% to ~$100, UST 10Y 4.35%, Bund below 3%; ECB pricing trimmed to two hikes (June 75%), BoE to ~50bp; Czech April CPI 2.5%.

calendar.plan_text: MoF May plan (30 Apr): sale auctions on 13 May (PLN 6-12bn), 21 May (7-13bn) and 27 May (6-12bn) in OK0129 (new 2Y, replaces OK0128), NZ0331, PS0731, DS0436 and NZ0936; a 46-week T-bill on 8 May (3-6bn); no switch. ~49% of 2026 needs financed after the April sales.
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; March's sell-off broke it and April's auction days cheapened on average. Remaining May sales: 13 May, 21 May, 27 May. Next MPC 1-2 Jun: a hold is expected; the July projection is the next marker.

core_text: Regime: deal hopes versus stalemate - oil swinging around $100-110; the NBP held at 3.75% on 6 May while FRAs price roughly 55bp of NBP hikes; the ECB is priced for a June hike, the BoE for hikes, the Fed has turned to hike risk, the CNB and MNB are on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 52bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 263bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 6 May close). US-Iran memo hopes: Brent -7.6% to ~$100 (6 May).
